name: BREACH://
tagline: Break into a fictional version of SRATH's own systems from a terminal. Six missions, one access key.
description:
A puzzle game played entirely in a terminal. Tommy has challenged you to break into SRATH, and somewhere on its network is an access key split into five fragments. Explore the filesystem, uncover hidden files, decode Base64, scan servers for open ports, query the project database, break a cipher and get past the security system guarding root.

No programming knowledge needed: type help for the commands and hint when you get stuck. Most puzzles can be solved in more than one way, there are achievements for the creative routes, and a few easter eggs for anyone who types the classics. Your progress is saved in this browser, so you can come back and continue.

Everything in the game is made up and runs on this page only. These are not SRATH's real servers, and no real systems are touched.
tech: Plain JavaScript: one file, no frameworks or libraries
Simulated machine: a Unix-like filesystem with users and permissions, hosts and ports, processes and signals
A small SQL engine: SELECT with WHERE, AND/OR, LIKE, ORDER BY and LIMIT, written from scratch
Base64, Caesar and Vigenère ciphers, all computed in the browser
Shell features: tab completion, command history and Ctrl+C
localStorage: progress, achievements and history are saved in your browser
The vault page is generated by the site's own build script from its content files

name: Gridword
tagline: Guess the five-letter word in six tries. A new word every day.
description: A daily word puzzle. Guess the hidden five-letter word in six tries: teal tiles are letters in the right spot, indigo tiles are in the word but somewhere else. Everyone gets the same word each day, and a practice mode gives you as many extra words as you like.
tech: Plain JavaScript: no frameworks or libraries; the interface is HTML and CSS animations
Word lists: the public-domain ENABLE list for guesses, plus hand-picked answer words
Daily word: a seeded shuffle and the visitor's local date, so everyone gets the same word without a server
localStorage: statistics and streaks are saved in your browser
Web Share and Clipboard APIs: share your result without revealing the word

name: Trails
tagline: Steer a glowing dot that leaves a line behind it. Don't hit a line, and slip through the gaps.
description:
An arcade game for up to six dots. Each dot leaves a glowing line behind it, and you can only steer left and right, never sharply. Touch any line, including your own, and you are out. Every few seconds your line breaks for a moment: a ring closing around your dot warns you, and while the line is broken you can hop over other lines, while anyone can slip through your gap.

Power-ups add chaos if you want it: Ghost, Boost, Brake, Sharp turns and Wrap help you; Slow others and Fat lines hit everyone else; Clear and Shrink change the arena. Switch each one on or off before you start.

Play against computer dots, or with two players on one keyboard, in full screen if you like. Online play with friends on other machines is planned.
tech: Plain JavaScript and the HTML Canvas 2D API, no game engine
Fixed timestep: the game runs at 120 updates per second on a fixed arena, so it plays the same on every screen
Collision grid: lines are stamped into a grid with 2-unit cells for fast, exact hit tests
Computer players: they simulate the curved path of each possible move before choosing one
Web Audio API: sound effects are synthesised in the browser, with no audio files
Pointer Events, the Fullscreen API and localStorage for touch steering, full screen and saved settings
